correction: The post used plain `curl`, so a user's ~/.curlrc could add a header, follow a redirect or set a proxy on a report. curl now runs with `-q` (--disable) as its first argument, the only position where curl honors it.
evidence: Cross-review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) of c69cb30, blocking point 3. test/snosi-health-report-test.sh sets HOME, CURL_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a .curlrc with `header = "X-Leak: 1"` and `location`: "a .curlrc header never reaches the intake" fails without -q.
